title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC0RF_0RD0RB_1RE0RC_1LA0LA_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC0RF_0RD0RB_1RE0RC_1LA0LA_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a sequence of cycles. Cycle n starts at P 1^3 0^K 1 E>0 with a gap of K ≈ 3·2n zeros. Sweeps then fill the gap from the right, four 0s per sweep; one pass to the left end and one back rewrite the prefix P and open the next gap, K' = 2K − c. Lean proves the fill sweep and any number of them at once (kernel), and that the run from blank tape follows them. A C simulator that jumps over the fill sweeps runs 28 cycles, 1.06·1017 steps, with no halt; it agrees exactly with direct simulation through cycle 12. The prefix holds smaller gaps that grow by factors near 1.36 to 1.5 per cycle, an irregular hierarchy with no visible closed form.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: The fill sweep
claims.text: At an E-record L 0^(z+4) 1 0 1 1 1 0 (10)^m 1 E>0 with blank tape to the right, one sweep gives L 0^z 1 0 1 1 1 0 (10)^(m+4) 1 E>0 in 4m + 40 steps, for all z, m and every tape L (fill, from fill_raw by bbtools.symtm.prove). k sweeps at once take fcost k m = k(4m + 40) + 8k(k − 1) steps (fills).

claims.title: The run follows it
claims.text: From blank tape the machine is at the fill record with z = 95, m = 2 after 3,224 steps (reach3224, list simulator evaluated by the kernel), and 23 sweeps and 5,152 steps later at z = 3, m = 94 (reach_fill_end).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 83,723 cells have been visited and 34,684 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in 28 cycles, 1.06·10<sup>17</sup> steps
claims.text: c/cyc17.c simulates directly but rewrites the tape for all fill sweeps but the last two at once. Its cycle starts (step, K, whole prefix) agree with plain simulation through cycle 12 (25,164,855 steps). It ran to cycle 28 with no halt: 106,309,693,328,363,073 steps, K = 798,641,935, 9.99·109 steps simulated directly, before it ran out of its 1.5·109-cell tape.

claims.title: Shape of the cycles
claims.text: K goes 9, 15, 27, 51, 99, 197, 389, 773, …, 798641935: K' = 2K − c, where c is a few tens at first and grows with the prefix. The prefix (37,199 cells at cycle 28) alternates between two head forms. Its tail holds gaps of 0s, at cycle 28 0^313 1^3 0^711 1^3 0^36103; the largest grows by about 1.48 per cycle and the next ones by 1.36 to 1.5. New gaps appear and old ones merge. It halts only on B>1 1 (B1 goes to F, F1 halts), which would have to happen in one of the passes over the prefix.

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state A reading 0 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 2 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (24 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 15 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: No halting class among 785 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 785 contexts expanded, 785 found, to depth 23. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 355 contexts longer than 300 cells were not expanded.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The fill phase is understood and proved. The passes that rewrite the prefix are not: they act like a hierarchy of counters whose gaps grow at incommensurate rates, and no invariant is known that keeps B>1 1 away.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The machine works in cycles. Each cycle fills a long gap of 0s four cells at a time, then opens a new gap about twice as long and rewrites a short prefix that holds smaller gaps. Lean proves the filling. A simulator that jumps over it ran 28 cycles, 10<sup>17</sup> steps, without a halt.

facts.text: 4m + 40 steps per sweep, any number at once (Lean, kernel).
No halt in 28 cycles of the jumping simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Does any remainder class halt?
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state A reading 0 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 2 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 15 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 785 contexts expanded, 785 found, to depth 23. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 355 contexts longer than 300 cells were not expanded.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508).
After 109 steps the tape spans 83,723 cells (23 left of the start, 65,615 right), with a density of 1s of 0.414.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Cycles: a prefix and a gap
html: Watch the tape at the moments the head is in state E on a new cell at the right end. At the start of each cycle it reads P 1^3 0^K 1 E>0: a short prefix P, three 1s and a gap of K zeros. The first gaps are 9, 15, 27, 51, 99, 197, 389 and 773: each is nearly twice the one before.

sections.heading: Filling the gap
html: Within a cycle the right end reads 0^z 1 0 1 1 1 0 (10)^m 1 E>0. One sweep runs left to the gap and back. It takes four 0s off the gap and adds four 10 pairs, z → z − 4 and m → m + 4, in 4m + 40 steps. The prefix is not touched. Lean proves this for all z, m and every prefix (fill, fills), and checks that the run from blank tape is in this form at step 3,224.
So a gap of K costs about K/4 sweeps and K2/2 steps, and each cycle takes about four times as many steps as the one before.

sections.heading: Two passes and a hierarchy of gaps
html: When fewer than four 0s are left, one pass runs to the left end of the tape and one runs back. They rewrite the prefix and turn the (10)^m run into the next gap, K' = 2K − c. The prefix also holds gaps. They grow more slowly, by about 1.36 to 1.5 per cycle, and new ones appear while old ones merge. At cycle 28 (K = 798,641,935) the prefix is 37,199 cells long and ends 0^313 1^3 0^711 1^3 0^36103.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1, and F is entered only from B reading 1. So the machine halts exactly when B meets 1 1. The fill sweeps never do this. It would have to happen during a pass over the prefix, whose contents keep changing in an irregular way.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel: the fill sweep and k sweeps at once, with exact step counts, and the run from blank tape reaching them (lean/Macro.lean).
Lean, native_decide: no halt in the first 107 steps (lean/Blank.lean).
Computed: 28 cycles and 1.06·1017 steps without a halt (c/cyc17.c, which agrees with plain simulation through cycle 12).
Open: the passes over the prefix, and so the question.

family: doubling bouncer with a growing prefix of nested gaps
summary: Each cycle fills a gap of 0s four cells per sweep, and two passes then open a new gap about twice as long while rewriting a prefix of smaller gaps that grow by about 1.5 per cycle. Lean proves the fill sweeps; no halt in 28 cycles (1.06·10<sup>17</sup> steps) of a jumping simulator.
